title: Gabber strict-local torsion cohomological bound
statement: Let $m\ge1$ and let $\Lambda$ be a commutative $\mathbf Z/m\mathbf Z$-algebra (equivalently a commutative ring with $m\Lambda=0$). Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Assume that there is an integer $N\ge0$ such that every scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre] of $f$ has topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] at most $N$. For a geometric point $x$ of $X$ [def-weil-geometric-point], put $s=f(x)$ and let $f_{(x)}:X_{(x)}\to S_{(s)}$ be the induced morphism of strict localizations [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality]. On the small etale categories of constant-coefficient $\Lambda$-modules [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with higher direct images as in [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], for every sheaf $G$ on $X_{(x)}$ and every $q>2N$ one has $R^q f_{(x)*}G=0$ as a sheaf on $S_{(s)}$.

source.place: Corollary 1.15, with the hypotheses of Theorem 1.14 (PDF pp. 15–16); local PDF WANTED; published PDF read online.

proof.text: Write $T=X_{(x)}$, $B=S_{(s)}$, $j:T\to X$ and $h=f_{(x)}:T\to B$. Both $T$ and $B$ are affine by [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. An affine scheme is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated] applied to its structural map. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-separated-target-affine-morphism] makes $h$ affine, and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3) makes it qcqs. Put $A=\mathbf Z/m\mathbf Z$. Every $\Lambda$-sheaf $G$ has an underlying $A$-module sheaf $G_A$ with the same abelian sheaf, since $mG=0$. By [lem-sbc-higher-direct-image-forget-comparison] for $\Lambda$ and for $A$, the underlying abelian sheaves of $R^qh_*G$ and $R^qh_*G_A$ are isomorphic. Consequently it suffices to prove the assertion for $A$-module sheaves. Here $A$ is finite, even when $\Lambda$ is infinite.

source.place: Corollary 1.15: coefficient reduction and affine strict-local geometry; Stacks 01S7 (lemma-affine-separated)

proof.text:
We first prove the bound for $j^*F$ with $F$ any $A$-module sheaf on $X$. Fix $q>2N$. Apply [lem-trf-gabber-nearby-cycle-dimension-bound] with coefficient ring $A$: it gives $\mathcal H^qR\Psi_f(F[0])=0$. The integer, fibre bound and locally-finite-type hypothesis are exactly those of the item. Applying the point functor at any specialization triple $(x,s\leftarrow t_0)$ and then [lem-trf-oriented-point-cohomology] with second scheme $S$ and second morphism $1_S$ gives
$$H^q(T\times_B S_{(t_0)},F|_{T\times_B S_{(t_0)}})=0.$$
The specialization here is the supplied map $S_{(t_0)}\to B$. Taking cohomology after the point functor is legitimate: [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image] proves exactness for constant-module inverse image along any geometric morphism and its compatibility with forgetting scalars. The complex $F[0]$ is bounded below, as required by the oriented-point formula.

source.place: Theorem 1.14 and formula (1.3.1), the stalk form of (1.12.6)

proof.text: Let $\rho:B=S_{(s)}\to S$ be the structural map and let $t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to B$ be any geometric point; put $t_0=\rho t$, with this same algebraically closed field. We verify the local affine hypothesis of the current [lem-trf-ind-etale-strict-local-invariance]. By [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality](1), $B=\operatorname{Spec}H$ is local and its closed point maps to $s$. Choose an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $S$ containing $s$. Its inverse image contains the closed point of $B$, hence all of $B$: a basic open containing the maximal ideal of a local ring is defined by a unit. Thus $\rho$ factors through $V$. This factorization supplies a ring map $a:R\to H$, and [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-affine-chart-ind-etale], with the identity $\operatorname{Spec}H=B$, says $a$ is ind-etale. The whole affine $B$ and $V$ therefore verify the invariance lemma's hypothesis near every $t$, including nonclosed points. It gives the canonical isomorphism $e:B_{(t)}\xrightarrow{\sim}S_{(t_0)}$ over $S$. If $b:B_{(t)}\to B$ is the structural map, set $c=b e^{-1}:S_{(t_0)}\to B=S_{(s)}$. Since $e$ is over $S$, $c$ is an $S$-morphism and is precisely an allowed specialization in step 2. Moreover $ce=b$. The fibre-product universal property consequently identifies the tube in step 2 with $T\times_B B_{(t)}$, together with its projection to $T$. Thus the vanishing in step 2 applies to every strict-local stalk tube of $h$.

source.place: Tag 04HX (lemma-describe-etale-local-ring), the affine-chart ind-etale presentation, and the current ind-etale strict-local invariance statement; explicit specialization supplying Illusie (1.12.7).

proof.text: The strict-local stalk formula [prop-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-stalk-formula], applied to the qcqs morphism $h$ and the torsion underlying abelian sheaf of $j^*F$, identifies each stalk of its $q$-th abelian higher direct image with the zero group from step 3. To identify that group with the underlying group of module cohomology use [lem-pe-left-module-derived-evaluation-forget] at the final object of the Milnor tube; inverse images commute with forgetting by [lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image]. The higher-image forgetting comparison [lem-sbc-higher-direct-image-forget-comparison] now identifies these with the stalks of the forgotten $A$-module sheaf $R^qh_*j^*F$. Hence [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative], applied to its map to zero, gives $R^qh_*j^*F=0$. Forgetting the module action reflects the zero sheaf, since an abelian group with one element has a unique module structure.

source.place: Stacks 03Q9 (theorem-higher-direct-images); coefficient evaluation and geometric-stalk detection

proof.text: It remains to pass from restrictions to arbitrary sheaves on $T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], $T$ is qcqs, and the finite ring $A$ permits [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaf-colimit-constructible]: write $G_A=\varinjlim_\alpha C_\alpha$ over a small filtered category with every $C_\alpha$ constructible. The qcqs morphism $h$ satisfies the hypotheses of [lem-sbc-higher-direct-image-large-filtered-colimit], so $R^qh_*G_A=\varinjlim_\alpha R^qh_*C_\alpha$. We will show that each term on the right is zero by making $C_\alpha$ a retract of an ambient restriction. This use of finite coefficients is on $A$, not an unsupported finiteness assertion about $\Lambda$.

source.place: Stacks 03SA (lemma-torsion-colimit-constructible), finite-coefficient constructible approximation and filtered continuity

proof.text: Fix one constructible $A$-sheaf $C$ on $T$. In the affine pointed-neighbourhood limit of [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], all stages are qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. All transition maps are affine: their sources and targets are affine, so separatedness of the targets and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-separated-target-affine-morphism] apply. Use [lem-weil-pbc-cofiltered-limit-directed-reindex] to put this small cofiltered limit over a directed set without changing its limit or its stages. Then [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-module-limit-descent] gives a pointed affine etale neighbourhood $u:U\to X$, its canonical projection $a:T\to U$, and a constructible $A$-sheaf $C_U$ with $a^*C_U\cong C$. The projections satisfy $ua=j$. No assertion that an arbitrary $G_A$ descends to a single stage has been made.

source.place: Stacks 09YU (lemma-category-is-colimit), essential surjectivity for finite-ring module sheaves

proof.text: Form $P=T\times_XU$ with projections $v:P\to T$, $b:P\to U$. The map $\sigma=(1_T,a):T\to P$ is a section of $v$ because $ua=j$. The affine source $U$ makes $u$ separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-source-morphism-separated]. Its base change $v$ is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-base-change] and etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-clopen-immersion] identifies $\sigma$ with an open-and-closed component of $P$. In particular $P=\sigma(T)\amalg P_1$, with $v|_{\sigma(T)}$ the identity after that identification, and $\sigma^*b^*C_U=a^*C_U\cong C$.

source.place: Stacks 02GO (base change of etale maps); section of separated etale map is clopen

proof.text: Put $F=u_!C_U$, an $A$-module sheaf on $X$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-modules], $j^*F\cong v_!b^*C_U$. The clopen decomposition of step 7 splits this sheaf as $C\oplus E$, where $E=(v|_{P_1})_!((b^*C_U)|_{P_1})$. Here is the elementary splitting argument: for an etale test object over $T$, separate any lift to $P$ into its inverse images of the two clopen parts. These form a disjoint open cover. In the sum-extension formula [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension], the terms on the first part give $C$ and those on the second part give $E$. Sheaf gluing along this disjoint cover gives mutually inverse maps with $C\oplus E$. Inclusion of the first summand and projection back to it compose to $1_C$. Thus $C$ is a retract of $j^*F$.

source.place: Stacks 03S6 (lemma-shriek-base-change); explicit splitting over a disjoint clopen cover

proof.text: Apply $R^qh_*$ to the retraction $C\to j^*F\to C$. Functoriality preserves its composite $1_C$. Step 4 says $R^qh_*j^*F=0$, so the identity of $R^qh_*C$ factors through zero and is zero. Hence $R^qh_*C=0$. Step 5 now expresses $R^qh_*G_A$ as a colimit of zero objects, which is zero: the zero cocone has a unique map into every cocone. Finally step 1 identifies the underlying abelian sheaf of $R^qh_*G$ with zero, and hence $R^qh_*G=0$ as a $\Lambda$-module sheaf. The argument holds for every $G$ and $q>2N$. If $m=1$, every unital module sheaf is already zero; if $X$ has no geometric point, the asserted quantification is empty.
